hook: [act:hushed, drawing us in]Imagine the ^Sahara, but ^green, with a lake about the size of the Caspian ^Sea. [act:the big question, clear][tune:rise]So what does@verb the sand still ^remember? [act:bright, rolling up sleeves][tune:fall]Let's investigate ^eight cases, one by ^one.

cases.where: the Sahara, from Egypt to Mauritania
cases.t1: [act:storytelling, like a guide]First stop: the green ^Sahara, from about eleven to five thousand years ^ago.
cases.t2: [act:the question, leaning in][tune:rise]When the rains failed, did it switch off ^overnight?
cases.t3: [act:explaining]Ocean dust off Mauritania jumps within ^centuries. [act:the counterpoint]But a lake in Chad records@verb a slow change, over ^thousands of years.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]Switched off overnight: *mixed ^record@noun*. [act:fair, warm]The green Sahara itself is well ^established.

cases.where: the Great Sand Sea, Egypt and Libya
cases.evidence_note: the glass: c. 29 million years old
cases.t1: [act:storytelling, intrigued]On Tutankhamun's chest sits a yellow-green ^scarab, made of desert@noun ^glass.
cases.t2: [act:the claim, wide-eyed][tune:rise]Glass melted by something from ^space?
cases.t3: [p:0.9][act:explaining, building]Tiny crystals in it hold traces of a mineral made only in ^impacts: a fingerprint at the ^scene. [act:the catch, curious]But the crater is still ^missing.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]A jewel made by a cosmic impact: *strong ^evidence*.

cases.evidence_note: their lineage split: c. 50,000 years ago
cases.t1: [act:tender, storytelling]Two women who died about seven thousand years ago, in a green ^Sahara.
cases.t3: [p:0.9][act:explaining]Their DNA: a branch of the human family ^tree that split off some fifty thousand years ago, and stayed ^apart. [act:the point, clear]So the herders were mostly ^local.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]A lost lineage: *strong ^evidence*. [act:fair]But two people aren't a whole ^people.

cases.evidence_note: shafts: about 9 m deep on average
cases.t1: [act:storytelling, intrigued]The ^Garamantes: oasis towns, pyramid ^tombs, and hundreds of kilometres of ^tunnels.
cases.t3: [act:explaining, grave]Their tunnels tapped water that fell as rain in wetter ^times, and it doesn't come ^back. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture]Like savings with no ^income: one day, they're ^gone.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*^Plausible*: a leading explanation, not the only ^one.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling]^Nabta Playa, in Egypt: a stone circle only four metres across, from about {4800|forty-eight hundred} ^BCE.
cases.t3: [act:explaining, precise]Two gaps line up north to ^south; another faces the midsummer ^sunrise. [act:the catch]But the star dates fall some fifteen hundred years before the ^stones.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Mixed ^record@noun*: the ^sun, probably; the stars, a ^stretch.

cases.evidence_note: two phases, a long dry spell between
cases.t1: [act:tender, hushed]In ^Niger, by a vanished lake: a woman and two children, buried in an ^embrace.
cases.t2: [act:the question][tune:rise]Two phases of burials: two different ^peoples?
cases.t3: [act:explaining]In {2008|two thousand eight}, the team thought ^so. [act:the twist, precise]In {2025|twenty twenty-five}, a study of their teeth found them hard to tell ^apart.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling, intrigued]In one of the driest places on ^Earth, someone painted ^swimmers.
cases.t2: [act:the question, fair][tune:rise]A real ^lake, or the dead, in the waters before ^creation, as in later Egyptian ^tombs?
cases.t3: [act:the catch, precise]The paintings are two or three thousand years older than those tomb ^texts. [p:0.9][act:the everyday picture]Like explaining a Roman mosaic with a guidebook written ^today.
cases.t4: [act:the verdict, measured][tune:fall]*Open ^question*. [act:a small smile]The swimmers aren't telling ^yet.

cases.t1: [act:storytelling, playful]Last stop: ^Tassili, in Algeria, and a painted giant nicknamed the great Martian ^god.
cases.t2: [act:the claim, fair]Its round head is smooth and ^featureless. [act:the question][tune:rise]A ^helmet?
cases.t3: [act:explaining]Blank heads look like a ^convention: masks, body paint, or spirit ^beings. [act:grave, measured]The real scandal? [act:grave]Copyists wetted the paintings to brighten ^them, and they faded ^faster.

close: [act:stepping back, calm]So what do our eight cases say ^together?
[act:clear, warm]The Sahara isn't an empty space on the ^map.
[act:wonder]It's an ^archive of rain, genes, glass and ^paint, drying in the ^sun.
[act:tender, sincere][tune:fall]And its oldest stories are ^human ones: people who herded, painted, and loved their ^dead.
